close_reason: Ratified review observation. The manual Debug impl on SessionClient (mod.rs:133-143) is intentional credential-leak prevention — JmapClient holds the auth credential and jmap-base-client deliberately does not derive Debug; deriving Debug here would either fail to compile (good outcome) or, after some future #[derive(Debug)] on JmapClient, silently leak credentials into logs (bad outcome). The manual impl pins the redaction. No code change required. The follow-up canary-test recommendation is workspace-wide — applies identically to all 7 extension-client siblings (mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata) and to base-client itself; filing a separate workspace-wide bead would be appropriate. Not in scope of this single-crate review.
description: src/methods/mod.rs:133-143 implements Debug manually for SessionClient, showing 'client: <JmapClient>' instead of the real JmapClient internals. Reason: JmapClient holds an HTTP client containing the auth credential, and jmap-base-client intentionally does not derive Debug to avoid that leak. Deriving Debug here would either fail to compile (good) or, after a future #[derive(Debug)] on JmapClient, leak credentials into logs (bad). The manual impl pins the redaction in place. Defend against any future 'simplify by deriving Debug' suggestion — and against any future change to JmapClient that would make the derive 'just work'. This is consistent with the workspace per-type Debug redaction canary pattern (workspace AGENTS.md §Security testing). A canary test asserting that a bearer-token literal doesn't appear in format!("{sc:?}") output would harden this guarantee further; tracking separately would be appropriate.
title: SessionClient manual Debug impl redacts the inner JmapClient
